# Using libtmux for Haskell

Capture an existing tmux endpoint, then process detached records with ordinary
Haskell. Start with the complete [capture program](../README.md), then read
[observation and recovery semantics](capture.md) and the [API guide](api.md).

| Task | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Add the source package to a Cabal application | [Installation](installation.md) |
| Capture, filter and traverse the object graph | [Observations and recovery](capture.md) |
| Inspect typed selections and check physical or contextual uniqueness | [Typed queries](query.md) |
| Share resources across independent Server scopes | [Shared Runtime](shared-runtime.md) |
| Test application predicates without tmux | [Validated offline fixtures](fixtures.md) |
| Reproduce capture measurements | [Performance](performance.md) |
| Parse IDs, validate geometry and admit a release | [Typed values](values.md) |
| Browse modules, declarations and source | [API documentation](api.md) |
| Decide whether the current package meets your needs | [Implementation status](status.md) |

The [behavior contracts](contracts/README.md) describe the implementation
scope. They include operations that are not yet public APIs.

The accepted [native domain model ADR](decisions/0001-native-domain-model.md)
records the physical graph, naming, lifecycle and public API decisions.

Repository setup and test authoring live in
[contributing](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and
[testing](../.github/TESTING.md).

# Add the package to a Cabal application

The [package manifest](../libtmux-haskell.cabal) declares the language edition
and dependency compatibility bounds. Use a current GHC and Cabal that satisfy
those bounds. The native backend requires Linux x86_64; see its
[host requirements](#native-backend-host-requirements).
[Contributor setup](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain) links the CI pins for
reproducing the tested configuration.

Pin the reviewed source revision in your application's `cabal.project`:

<!-- example-project: capture-graph -->
```cabal
packages: .
index-state: 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z

source-repository-package
  type: git
  location: https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell
  tag: e9318e703a56547646d6978d880575862200f4e1
```

Add the library to the executable's dependencies. The
[example package](../examples/capture-graph/libtmux-capture-graph.cabal) is a
complete starting point:

<!-- example-package: capture-graph -->
```cabal
cabal-version: 3.18
name: libtmux-capture-graph
version: 0.0.0
build-type: Simple
license: MIT
extra-doc-files: README.md

executable capture-graph
  main-is: Main.hs
  default-language: GHC2024
  ghc-options: -Wall -Werror
  build-depends:
    base >=4.22 && <4.23,
    filepath >=1.5.4 && <1.6,
    libtmux-haskell ^>=0.1.0.0,
    text >=2.1.3 && <2.2
```

Save [Main.hs](../examples/capture-graph/Main.hs) beside the package file, then
download the package index before the first build:

```console
$ cabal update
```

Use the [private demonstration server](../README.md) from the README, then
run the Haskell executable:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 capture-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

The [capture guide](capture.md) explains the object graph, pure lookups and
scope cleanup. Its owned fixture creates a repeatable server for the
[README example](../README.md). Enable
[`OverloadedRecordDot`](https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/9.14.1/docs/users_guide/exts/overloaded_record_dot.html)
in application
modules using observation fields. No optics or effect framework is required.

The package has no Hackage release yet. The development source provides the
observation API; commands and workspace tooling remain under development.
Check [status](status.md) before choosing it for automation.

## Native backend host requirements

The native backend targets Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or newer
for `pidfd_spawn`, compatible kernel pidfd operations, and exclusive child
reaping ownership. Missing host operations fail before launch. This is
separate from pure scalar construction and lookup. See the
[process host contract](contracts/process.md#launch-and-host-requirements).

# Capture and navigate a tmux server

Use [`withServer`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to adopt an existing endpoint and
[`capture`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to obtain a detached
[`Snapshot`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs). The complete program in the
[README](../README.md) filters ordinary pane records, traverses relationships
and prints its result after the handle closes. Its
[source](../examples/capture-graph/Main.hs) and
[owned fixture verification](../scripts/check_sdist.py) are checked from the
source archive, with output asserted and owned process exits observed.

Create the [private demonstration server](../README.md) from the README, then
run the Haskell executable from a provisioned checkout:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 capture-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

To inspect your own running server, pass its actual socket and executable
paths instead. The program observes that daemon; it does not create or stop it.

The library requires a trusted absolute socket path and a writable pin
directory on that socket's filesystem. The default pin directory is the
socket's parent. [Installation](installation.md#native-backend-host-requirements)
describes the Linux host requirements.

## Physical entities and appearances

A session links windows at numeric indices. The same physical window can
appear at two indices in one session or in several sessions. A pane belongs
to its physical window, while a pane occurrence retains the window-link
context:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["Session demo"] --> L0["WindowLink index 0"]
    S --> L4["WindowLink index 4"]
    L0 --> W["Window @0"]
    L4 --> W
    W --> P["Pane %0"]
```

`windows` and `panes` return each physical entity once. `windowLinks` and
`paneOccurrences` retain both appearances in this fixture. Lists use numeric
ID order; links use session ID and window index; occurrences use link and
pane index. Indexed lookups avoid rescanning those lists.

References compare targeting identity within one Server generation. A lookup
returns the observation from the supplied snapshot, including a later capture
from that same Server. Independent Server scopes have distinct generations.
Resolving a native ID with `lookupPaneId` deliberately selects its observation
in the supplied snapshot; it does not restore an earlier targeting guarantee.

Record updates create local values. They do not update the snapshot's indexes,
validate a caller-edited graph or send a tmux command. Use
`dimensionValue pane.width` for numeric comparisons; checked dimensions have
no [`Num`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Prelude.html#t:Num)
instance. Paths and current process names preserve POSIX bytes;
window labels use `TmuxText` with explicit, fallible text conversion.

## Errors and recovery

Acquisition fails in `IO` with `TmuxException`. Pure navigation returns
`Either LookupError`; missing or foreign references never become empty results.
The snapshot records a monotonic capture interval. It does not claim a
transaction over tmux and operating-system state.

`withServer` preserves a callback's original exception, including cancellation.
If bounded cleanup remains incomplete, its exception context retains a
`CleanupRecovery`. After a successful callback, incomplete cleanup raises
`CleanupFailed` instead of returning success.

Use `tryTmux` to catch library failures with their
[`ExceptionWithContext`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Control-Exception.html#t:ExceptionWithContext),
or [`Control.Exception.tryWithContext`](https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/base-4.22.0.0/docs/Control-Exception.html#v:tryWithContext)
when handling application exceptions and
cancellation too. Ordinary typed `try` loses this context when returning the
concrete exception. Keep the context while recovering ownership.

`cleanupRecoveries` and `captureRecoveries` retrieve correlated owners from
that context. Inspect them locally, resume existing cleanup, or explicitly
detach logical uncertainty. Resuming never dispatches a second capture;
detachment does not terminate native resources or prove daemon-side completion.
The [process contract](contracts/process.md) defines these outcomes in detail.

Use [validated offline fixtures](fixtures.md) to exercise application graph
logic without tmux. Their references belong to a separate offline origin.

The [capture baseline](performance.md) covers controlled graph sizes. The
[shared Runtime guide](shared-runtime.md) covers independent handle lifetimes.
Broader performance cases remain qualification work for the public observation
milestone. The
[status page](status.md) records the broader implementation scope.

The example fixture verifies daemon exit after setup failure before session
dispatch, and both daemon and pane exit after callback failure or cancellation.
The runner joins interrupted session clients. When creation was dispatched but
the pane receipt is unavailable, it reports that incomplete ownership explicitly.

# Select observations with typed queries

Use [`runQuery`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) when a predicate needs inspection,
typed fields or relationship composition. It reads an existing
[`Snapshot`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot.hs) and returns ordinary lists inside
`Either QueryError`. Native comprehensions and `filter` remain the unrestricted
path for application logic; see the [capture program](capture.md).

This program finds active panes at least 120 cells wide. It compares the
typed selection with a native predicate over the same snapshot, checks
uniqueness, follows session-to-link-to-pane relationships, and inspects the
required fields. The fixture links one window at indices 0 and 4: one
physical pane therefore appears twice in the contextual source.

Create the [private demonstration server](../README.md) from the README. From a
[provisioned checkout](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain), run:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 query-graph -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

CI runs the installed program against an owned fixture, asserts output and
empty stderr, and observes the server and initial pane exiting afterward.
The program accepts an existing socket and tmux executable. Every
query construction and selection below is pure except the explicitly named
[`capture`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) and [`fetch`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs).

<!-- example: query-graph -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Query one detached graph, then distinguish physical and contextual matches.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (ExceptionWithContext, rethrowIO)
import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import Data.Function ((&))
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Query qualified as Q
import LibTmux.Query.Link qualified as Link
import LibTmux.Query.Occurrence qualified as Occurrence
import LibTmux.Query.Pane qualified as Pane
import LibTmux.Query.Session qualified as Session
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path

data ApplicationError
  = OperationalFailure (ExceptionWithContext Tmux.TmuxException)
  | InvalidQuery Q.QueryError
  | InvalidSelection Q.CardinalityError
  | UnexpectedResult String

activeWide :: Q.Expr Tmux.Pane
activeWide = Q.allOf [Q.eq Pane.active True, Q.dimensionAtLeast Pane.width 120]

selectedPanes :: Q.Query Tmux.Pane
selectedPanes = Q.panes & Q.matching activeWide

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
    acquired <- Tmux.tryTmux $ Tmux.withServer config $ \server -> do
      snapshot <- Tmux.capture server
      fresh <- Q.fetch server selectedPanes
      pure (snapshot, fresh)
    case first OperationalFailure acquired >>= uncurry report of
      Left (OperationalFailure problem) -> rethrowIO problem
      Left (InvalidQuery problem) -> die ("Query validation failed: " <> show problem)
      Left (InvalidSelection problem) -> die ("Selection failed: " <> show problem)
      Left (UnexpectedResult problem) -> die problem
      Right linesToPrint -> mapM_ putStrLn linesToPrint
  _ -> die "Usage: query-graph SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"

report :: Tmux.Snapshot -> Either Q.QueryError [Tmux.Pane] -> Either ApplicationError [String]
report snapshot acquired = do
  selected <- first InvalidQuery (Q.runQuery snapshot selectedPanes)
  let native = [pane | pane <- Tmux.panes snapshot, pane.active, Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width >= 120]
  if selected == native then Right () else Left (UnexpectedResult "query and native selection disagree")
  unique <- first InvalidSelection (Q.exactlyOne selected)
  occurrences <- first InvalidQuery $ Q.runQuery snapshot $
    Q.paneOccurrences & Q.matching (Q.related Occurrence.pane activeWide)
  highest <- first InvalidQuery $ Q.runQuery snapshot $
    Q.windowLinks & Q.orderBy [Q.descending Link.index] & Q.limit 1
  link <- first InvalidSelection (Q.exactlyOne highest)
  let containingEditors = Q.sessions & Q.matching (Q.some Session.windowLinks (Q.some Link.panes activeWide))
  sessions <- first InvalidQuery (Q.runQuery snapshot containingEditors)
  fresh <- first InvalidQuery acquired
  Right
    [ "query agrees with native predicate: True"
    , "unique physical pane: " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId unique.ref))
    , "contextual matches: " <> show (length occurrences)
    , "contextual uniqueness: " <> either show (const "unique") (Q.exactlyOne occurrences)
    , "highest link index: " <> show (Tmux.windowIndexValue link.index)
    , "sessions containing a match: " <> show (length sessions)
    , "required fields: " <> show (Q.requirements selectedPanes).fieldNames
    , "required relationships: " <> show (Q.requirements containingEditors).relationshipNames
    , "fresh capture matches: " <> show (length fresh)
    ]
```

Expected output:

<!-- example-output: query-graph -->
```text
query agrees with native predicate: True
unique physical pane: %0
contextual matches: 2
contextual uniqueness: AtLeastTwoMatches
highest link index: 4
sessions containing a match: 1
required fields: ["pane.active","pane.width"]
required relationships: ["session.windowLinks","windowLink.panes"]
fresh capture matches: 1
```

## Choose the source before checking cardinality

[`panes`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) selects unique physical panes.
[`paneOccurrences`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) selects their appearances through
window links. Filtering preserves the chosen source's multiplicity.
`exactlyOne` rejects no matches and reports `AtLeastTwoMatches` at the second
match; it does not count the remaining list. `atMostOne` also permits absence.
Proving uniqueness may still require traversing every input element.

[`some`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) tests one related child against its entire
predicate. Put all required conditions inside that child predicate when one
pane must satisfy them together. Two separate existential predicates may
match different panes. Over a known empty relation, `some` is false, `every`
is true and `none` is true. Missing required lookups remain errors.
`optionalRelated` is false for a known absent target; its negation includes
absence. An unavailable relationship is a validation error, even on an empty
source or in a branch that would otherwise short-circuit.

## Inspect, order and limit

The qualified [field modules](api.md) expose typed tokens from the capture
catalogue. Boolean fields cannot take numeric comparisons, and fields from
different row types cannot be mixed. `dimensionAtLeast` accepts an unbounded
`Integer` threshold while observed dimensions retain their checked type.
Text equality and containment are exact, without case folding or Unicode
normalization. Command names, paths and window labels retain their declared
byte-preserving types; there is no implicit text conversion.

[`requirements`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) reports stable source, field and
relationship names, ordering keys and the final limit. This is dependency
inspection, not serialization or a backend execution plan. Validation checks
all declared requirements before examining rows, including ordering keys,
empty membership predicates and zero limits.

`matching` accumulates predicates. `orderBy` replaces the ordering keys and
uses stable sorting; tied rows keep source order. `limit` replaces the final
nonnegative `Natural` bound. Evaluation always filters, orders and then
limits, regardless of builder order. Every authored description and operand
list must be finite.

## Keep acquisition and failures explicit

[`fetch`](../src/LibTmux/Query.hs) captures a new complete snapshot on every
call. It checks compiled evaluator support before acquisition, then validates
version requirements against captured metadata. This implementation performs
no backend filtering. Reuse `runQuery` over one snapshot when several
selections should share observations; see [capture costs](performance.md).

The example combines operational exceptions, pure query errors and
cardinality errors in an application error type. `tryTmux` catches library
exceptions only. Its handler preserves the exception context with `rethrowIO`,
keeping cleanup and capture recovery owners reachable; asynchronous
cancellation propagates. See [recovery](capture.md) when an application needs
to inspect and resume those owners.

The report reads detached values after the Server closes. Its equality check
uses one snapshot. The final fresh-capture count demonstrates another
acquisition; two independently changing captures do not prove evaluator
equivalence. Cardinality and reference equality establish observed selection,
not current liveness. Public mutation, query interchange, backend optimization
and event subscriptions remain [unfinished](status.md).

For a separate application, copy the [program](../examples/query-graph/Main.hs)
and [package file](../examples/query-graph/libtmux-query-graph.cabal), then use
its [immutable source dependency](../examples/query-graph/cabal.project.vcs)
with the [installation instructions](installation.md).

# Share a Runtime across independent Server scopes

Use [`withRuntime`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to give several components one
resource and cleanup owner. Open their endpoints with
[`withServerIn`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs). Closing one Server scope releases
that handle while the others remain usable under the shared limits.

Create the [private demonstration server](../README.md) from the README, then
run this complete program from a provisioned checkout. CI also runs it from
an installed package, checks output and observes owned process cleanup:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 shared-runtime -- \
    "$LIBTMUX_DEMO_DIR/s" \
    "$(command -v tmux)"
```

<!-- example: shared-runtime -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}

-- | Share Runtime resources while keeping Server lifetimes independent.
module Main (main) where

import Control.Exception (ExceptionWithContext (..))
import Control.Monad (forM_, unless)
import Data.Text qualified as Text
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import System.Environment (getArgs)
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsPath.Posix qualified as Path

main :: IO ()
main = getArgs >>= \case
  [socketArgument, executableArgument] -> do
    socket <- Path.encodeFS socketArgument
    executable <- Path.encodeFS executableArgument
    let config = (Tmux.serverConfig socket) {Tmux.executable = executable}
    snapshot <- Tmux.withRuntime $ \runtime ->
      Tmux.withServerIn runtime config $ \outer -> do
        first <- Tmux.capture outer
        closed <- Tmux.withServerIn runtime config $ \inner -> do
          unless (Tmux.serverGeneration inner /= Tmux.serverGeneration outer) $
            fail "independent handles shared a connection generation"
          captured <- Tmux.capture inner
          case Tmux.panes captured of
            pane : _ -> unless (Tmux.lookupPane first pane.ref == Left Tmux.ForeignGeneration) $
              fail "a reference crossed independent handle generations"
            [] -> fail "the owned example fixture has no pane"
          pure inner
        Tmux.tryTmux (Tmux.capture closed) >>= \case
          Left (ExceptionWithContext _ Tmux.ServerClosed) -> pure ()
          Left problem -> fail ("closed handle returned an unexpected error: " <> show problem)
          Right _ -> fail "the inner handle remained open after its scope"
        Tmux.capture outer
    putStrLn "independent handles: verified"
    putStrLn "closed inner handle: rejected"
    putStrLn $ "outer capture panes: " <> show (length (Tmux.panes snapshot))
    forM_ (Tmux.panes snapshot) $ \pane -> do
      window <- either (fail . show) pure (Tmux.lookupWindow snapshot pane.window)
      putStrLn $ "detached pane " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId pane.ref))
        <> " belongs to " <> Text.unpack (Tmux.renderWindowId (Tmux.windowId window.ref))
  _ -> die "Usage: shared-runtime SOCKET TMUX_EXECUTABLE"
```

The program checks that references remain connection-scoped, the inner handle
closes, the outer handle still captures, and detached navigation works after
the entire Runtime closes.

<!-- example-output: shared-runtime -->
```text
independent handles: verified
closed inner handle: rejected
outer capture panes: 1
detached pane %0 belongs to @0
```

## Use the installed package

The core remains unpublished. This example's project pins the source that
provides the shared Runtime API. Use that project when building the standalone
program, together with its package file:

<!-- example-project: shared-runtime -->
```cabal
packages: .
index-state: 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z

source-repository-package
  type: git
  location: https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-haskell
  tag: 8b60ec5b60b0e4b0346c56122666ad26feb072ff
```

<!-- example-package: shared-runtime -->
```cabal
cabal-version: 3.18
name: libtmux-shared-runtime
version: 0.0.0
build-type: Simple
license: MIT
extra-doc-files: README.md

executable shared-runtime
  main-is: Main.hs
  default-language: GHC2024
  ghc-options: -Wall -Werror
  build-depends:
    base >=4.22 && <4.23,
    filepath >=1.5.4 && <1.6,
    libtmux-haskell ^>=0.1.0.0,
    text >=2.1.3 && <2.2
```

[Installation](installation.md) covers the compiler and native host setup.
The [archive consumer check](../scripts/check_sdist.py) builds the program
outside the checkout and executes it with the same owned fixture.

## Scope and recovery

Each adoption has a distinct generation, including handles to the same daemon.
A reference from one handle does not target another handle's observations.
Closing the Runtime also closes handles still retained by application tasks;
applications own their worker lifetimes. Starting another adoption after the
Runtime closes raises `RuntimeClosed`. Closing either kind of scope leaves
the tmux daemon running.

Limits belong to the Runtime. The current complete-capture reservation admits
one complete capture at a time; concurrent attempts can fail with an
operational capacity error. Capture sequentially or use independent Runtime
scopes when separate capacity is required. The
[performance guide](performance.md) records the measured workload and the
broader qualification still outstanding.

Use [`tryTmux`](../src/LibTmux/Server.hs) to keep the failure's exception
context. `cleanupRecoveries` retrieves its remaining cleanup owners. Their
inspection, retry, explicit wait and logical detachment stay scoped to the
selected responsibility. A failed adoption can retain an owner before it
returns a Server; recovering it does not close neighboring handles.

Nested scopes may contribute overlapping recovery owners. Inspect and resume
each retained responsibility. An explicit cleanup wait has no deadline;
cancellation preserves its owner. Detaching logical uncertainty does not
release native resources or prove a daemon-side command completed.
[Capture recovery](capture.md#errors-and-recovery) and the
[process contract](contracts/process.md#public-scope-outcomes) define the error
and cancellation policy.

# Test graph logic without tmux

Use [`LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture`](../src/LibTmux/Snapshot/Fixture.hs) to build
ordinary observation records and validate their relationships. No fixture
operation starts tmux, opens a socket or allocates an operational Server.

The complete program below tests a pane-selection policy against one physical
window appearing at two session indices. Run it from a provisioned checkout:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 offline-graph
```

For a separate Cabal application, copy [Main.hs](../examples/offline-graph/Main.hs)
and its [package file](../examples/offline-graph/libtmux-offline-graph.cabal).
Save the [pinned source project](../examples/offline-graph/cabal.project.vcs)
as `cabal.project`, provision its dependencies, then run the same command.

<!-- example: offline-graph -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedRecordDot #-}
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Test a pane-selection policy without starting tmux or opening a socket.
module Main (main) where

import Data.Bifunctor (first)
import LibTmux qualified as Tmux
import LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture qualified as F
import System.Exit (die)
import System.OsString.Posix qualified as Os

main :: IO ()
main = do
  snapshot <- either die pure buildSnapshot
  print (Tmux.snapshotOrigin snapshot)
  print
    [ (Tmux.renderPaneId (Tmux.paneId pane.ref), Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width)
    | pane <- Tmux.panes snapshot
    , pane.active
    , Tmux.dimensionValue pane.width >= 120
    ]
  print (length (Tmux.windows snapshot), length (Tmux.paneOccurrences snapshot))

buildSnapshot :: Either String Tmux.Snapshot
buildSnapshot = do
  version <- checked (Tmux.parseVersion "3.8")
  sid <- checked (Tmux.parseSessionId "$1")
  wid <- checked (Tmux.parseWindowId "@2")
  pid <- checked (Tmux.parsePaneId "%3")
  width <- checked (Tmux.mkDimension 120)
  height <- checked (Tmux.mkDimension 40)
  paneIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkPaneIndex 0)
  firstIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkWindowIndex 0)
  secondIndex <- checked (Tmux.mkWindowIndex 4)
  let origin = F.fixtureOrigin "reports"
      session = Tmux.Session (F.sessionRef origin sid) "work" 0
      window = Tmux.Window (F.windowRef origin wid) "editor" width height
      pane = Tmux.Pane
        { Tmux.ref = F.paneRef origin pid
        , Tmux.window = window.ref
        , Tmux.index = paneIndex
        , Tmux.width = width
        , Tmux.height = height
        , Tmux.active = True
        , Tmux.dead = False
        , Tmux.title = "editor"
        , Tmux.currentCommand = Os.fromBytestring "ghci"
        , Tmux.currentPath = Os.fromBytestring "/offline/project"
        }
      input = (F.emptyFixture origin version)
        { F.sessions = [session], F.windows = [window], F.panes = [pane]
        , F.windowLinks = [Tmux.WindowLink session.ref firstIndex window.ref True,
                          Tmux.WindowLink session.ref secondIndex window.ref False]
        }
  checked (F.validateFixture origin input)

checked :: Show problem => Either problem value -> Either String value
checked = first show
```

Program output:

<!-- example-output: offline-graph -->
```text
DefinedOffline "reports"
[("%3",120)]
(1,2)
```

`fixtureOrigin` creates a named offline namespace. Reuse a name to model
successive observations in one test scenario; use different names for
independent scenarios. Fixture references never compare equal to references
from an adopted Server, even when their native IDs match.

`emptyFixture` supplies synthetic server metadata and empty collections.
Populate its ordinary records, then call `validateFixture`. It reuses graph
and metadata validation, including reference membership, duplicate slots,
active selections and attached-client context. A failed input returns
`FixtureError`; it never becomes an empty snapshot. Reading an edited record
alone does not validate the graph or update a previously built snapshot.
Wire decoding, tmux's field normalization and transport limits apply to live
acquisition. Synthetic values can exercise cases a live capture cannot produce.

`SnapshotOrigin` distinguishes `DefinedOffline` from `AcquiredFromTmux`.
Offline snapshots have no acquisition interval. Neither provenance nor an
opaque reference proves that a tmux target is currently alive.

The [installed consumer check](../scripts/check_sdist.py) compiles this source
against the archived public package and asserts its output. The Hspec cases
exercise namespace separation and invalid graphs without a daemon. See
[capture and recovery](capture.md) for observations acquired from tmux.

# Typed tmux values

[Run the complete example](../examples/typed-values/Main.hs) from a checkout:

```console
$ cabal run --verbose=0 typed-values
```

The complete program uses only pure domain constructors before printing:

<!-- example: typed-values -->
```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

-- | Construct tmux domain values without starting a process
-- or contacting a server.
module Main (main) where

import LibTmux.Id (parseWindowId, renderWindowId)
import LibTmux.Value (dimensionValue, mkDimension)
import LibTmux.Version (parseVersion, renderVersion, requireSupported)

main :: IO ()
main = do
  version <- either (fail . show) pure $
    parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported
  window <- either (fail . show) pure (parseWindowId "@17")
  width <- either (fail . show) pure (mkDimension 120)
  print (renderVersion version, renderWindowId window, dimensionValue width)
```

Program output:

<!-- example-output: typed-values -->
```text
("3.3a","@17",120)
```

The program parses supplied text and constructs values. Its only `IO` prints
the result; it neither inspects an installed tmux binary nor contacts a server.

## IDs and indices describe different things

[`SessionId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs), [`WindowId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs) and [`PaneId`](../src/LibTmux/Id.hs) are distinct types. Their parsers require
the corresponding `$`, `@` or `%` prefix, canonical decimal spelling and the
native unsigned 32-bit range. Leading zeroes and whitespace are rejected.
Use the rendering functions when producing external target text.

An ID alone carries no endpoint or server lifetime. Parsing `@17` does not
prove that a window exists. Generation-bound references come from a validated
[snapshot](capture.md), where lookups retain the Server adoption's identity.

[`WindowIndex`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs) identifies a window link's position within a session.
[`PaneIndex`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs) identifies a pane's position within its window. Neither is an
entity ID. A physical window may have several links, including multiple
indices in the same session.

## Validate values where they enter the program

Constructors return `Either`: dimensions must be positive; indices must be
nonnegative. Their numeric accessors return `Integer`, so reading a value
does not narrow it to a machine-sized integer.

[`mkDimension`](../src/LibTmux/Value.hs) checks the mathematical domain. A particular tmux command can
impose a smaller numeric range; successful construction does not establish
that command's capability or maximum.

## Release admission has a limited meaning

[`parseVersion`](../src/LibTmux/Version.hs) accepts stable releases and the output format of `tmux -V`,
including one final LF. Development versions and trailing data are rejected.
[`requireSupported`](../src/LibTmux/Version.hs) admits the inclusive range from
tmux 3.3a through 3.8. Intermediate releases are supported; CI tests the endpoints.

These functions validate the supplied release identity. They do not inspect
the host or qualify all features of that release. See
[implementation status](status.md) for the boundary between the exposed
package and the transport work.

The [API guide](api.md) links the public modules and their error types.

# Measure capture cost

The capture benchmark measures the public `capture` operation, including
response decoding, graph validation, stored indexes and forcing owned values.
Endpoint adoption, fixture construction, derived occurrence counting and
teardown stay outside that timing. Each sample uses the default two-second
capture timeout.

Build the optional benchmark after provisioning the selected Haskell tools
and dependencies:

```console
$ cabal build bench:capture --offline
```

Run the three workloads against a selected tmux binary. The output directory
must be new; it receives raw CSV samples, host context and a JSON summary:

```console
$ python3 bench/capture.py \
    --tmux "$(command -v tmux)" \
    --output .cache/capture-benchmark
```

Repeat `--tmux` to compare binaries in one sweep. The reference run uses the
support endpoints, 3.3a and 3.8. Benchmarks form a separate tier and do not run
in routine test loops or add intermediate releases to CI.

The [Haskell harness](../bench/Capture.hs) uses the public interface.
The [fixture driver](../bench/capture.py) owns a foreground daemon and tracks
every created pane with a pidfd. It verifies graph cardinalities and observes
owned exits before accepting a result. Medium and large cases link three
physical windows across sessions; every case also retains two appearances
of the initial window.

## Reference run

The [recorded samples](../bench/results/capture-2026-11-08.json) were measured
on 2026-11-08 with GHC 9.14.1, Cabal 3.18.2.0, the library's default `-O1`
build and one RTS capability. The shared Linux host used a four-core CPU quota
and an 8 GiB process-group memory limit. Setup and teardown completed for all
six cases.

| tmux | Sessions | Physical windows | Physical panes | Median capture | Maximum capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3.3a | 1 | 3 | 6 | 3.1 ms | 5.5 ms |
| 3.3a | 5 | 25 | 75 | 10.5 ms | 12.3 ms |
| 3.3a | 15 | 80 | 250 | 41.4 ms | 49.7 ms |
| 3.8 | 1 | 3 | 6 | 4.7 ms | 5.2 ms |
| 3.8 | 5 | 25 | 75 | 11.7 ms | 12.8 ms |
| 3.8 | 15 | 80 | 250 | 28.3 ms | 29.8 ms |

Each row contains five samples, including the first capture in its Server
scope. Values are rounded up to a tenth of a millisecond. The JSON retains
exact elapsed and acquisition-interval nanoseconds, Haskell process CPU time,
cardinalities, source identities and host load. Haskell CPU time excludes
the daemon and command-client processes.

These measurements qualify the stated fixtures on this host. Allocations,
concurrent captures, active selection or geometry changes, long fields,
cancellation latency and other hosts remain separate qualification work.
Use the raw samples when comparing a change; a successful small sweep does
not establish a service-level latency guarantee.

Build the native Haddock browser from a checkout:

```console
$ cabal haddock lib:libtmux-haskell --offline
```

Prepare a separate browser copy with checked local navigation:

```console
$ python3 scripts/prepare_haddock.py \
    dist-newstyle/haddock-prepared \
    --build-plan dist-newstyle/cache/plan.json
```

The destination must be new; choose another directory or remove your previous
generated copy before preparing it again. The command selects the configured
library from Cabal's plan and leaves Cabal's original output untouched.

Serve the copy over HTTP so Quick Jump can load its search index:

```console
$ python3 -m http.server 8000 \
    --bind 127.0.0.1 \
    --directory dist-newstyle/haddock-prepared
```

Open [the local API browser](http://127.0.0.1:8000/).
Module overviews explain the types; declarations specify input domains, results and
errors. The project enables declaration-to-source links, interactive symbol
search and a Hoogle index for this package. Acquisition and recovery are
explicit `IO`; field access, list processing, parsers and navigation are pure.
Record fields use
[`OverloadedRecordDot`](https://downloads.haskell.org/ghc/9.14.1/docs/users_guide/exts/overloaded_record_dot.html);
the library does not generate
top-level selector functions. Detached record constructors support patterns
and local updates. Snapshot assembly and targeting references remain opaque.
For an ambiguous record update, qualify the field through its defining module.
For example, import `LibTmux.Server` as `Server` and update `Server.socketPath`;
this identifies the field owner without deprecated type-directed disambiguation.

The copy repairs navigation in Haddock 2.33.0's output: repeated record labels have
distinct owner-qualified anchors, and instance methods have local targets.
A name-only field link offers its record owners; a source identifier on
several lines offers those lines. Missing hidden-module instance attributions
retain their text and valid Source links. No private API page is added.
In the default theme, long module headings wrap and wide constructor,
instance and symbol-index sections scroll within the page on narrow screens.
Source listings use the mobile viewport and keep horizontal scrolling inside
a keyboard-focusable code region. Type annotations remain visible outside
the scrolling region and stay within the viewport. Native annotation behavior
remains available without the source enhancement. Source text and identifier
targets retain their native contents.

`navigation.json` records raw and prepared file digests and edit counts.
The check rejects missing local targets, browser assets and unexpected duplicate
IDs, including index and search links. It preserves signatures, instances, source text and
compiled interfaces. It does not verify external dependency URLs, prove that
an arbitrary raw directory is fresh, or publish anything. CI builds from its
checked-out source and retains the raw and prepared artifacts separately.

# Implementation status

Use the current source for detached observations and typed input values.
The package is unpublished. Public mutation commands are not implemented.

| Component | Available to consumers |
| --- | --- |
| Entity ID parsing/rendering | Yes, through `LibTmux.Id` |
| Checked dimensions and indices | Yes, through `LibTmux.Value` |
| Stable-release parsing and supported-range admission | Yes, through `LibTmux.Version` |
| Server, complete captures and generation-bound references | Implemented through `LibTmux.Server` and `LibTmux.Snapshot` |
| Bounded scope cleanup and correlated recovery | Implemented; keep exception context when catching failures |
| Validated offline fixtures | Implemented through `LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture` |
| Shared Runtime ownership | Implemented through `withRuntime` and `withServerIn`; see [the complete program](shared-runtime.md) |
| Typed predicates, relationships, ordering and cardinality | Implemented through `LibTmux.Query`; see [the complete program](query.md) |
| Mutation commands, query interchange and backend optimization | Not implemented |
| Control events, streams and cancellation API | Not implemented |
| Workspace library/CLI | Planned as a separate Cabal package using the core |
| MCP integration | Excluded from this port |

The [capture program](../examples/capture-graph/Main.hs) exercises the public
interface. Mutation, interchange, event and workspace contracts remain separate
qualification work.
The [behavior inventory](contracts/README.md) records the intended scope.

## Package policy

The core favors GHC boot libraries and ordinary `IO`. Additional dependencies
need a concrete requirement; JSON/YAML loading and command-line concerns
belong in the workspace package. MCP is outside this port's scope. See the
[package and dependency policy](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#package-and-dependency-policy).

## Compatibility evidence

CI uses the [recorded toolchain](../.tool-versions) on Linux x86_64. Its current
integration subset exercises owned fixtures, scalar framing, private socket
pins, public capture, scope recovery and process ownership with one and two
RTS capabilities on exact tmux
releases 3.3a and 3.8. The supported range includes all intermediate releases;
CI tests its endpoints.

The [workflow](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) and
[test guide](../.github/TESTING.md) describe those checks. This is evidence
for the implemented subset, not complete tmux API compatibility.

A [capture baseline](performance.md) records small, medium and large owned
graphs on both tmux endpoints. It measures the public API with raw samples
and host context. Allocation, concurrency and cancellation-latency
qualification remain open.
